messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2: Global traffic-shift job auto-triggered due to multiple AZ network flaps in us-west1. Pager sent to infra-oncall. Follow runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dr-failover

morgan: Seeing huge 5xx spike on /v1/generate and /v1/chat from us-west1 clients, started ~2139998700. Error type: 502 from edge LB. RTT also up from 120ms -> 900ms.

raj: Confirmed. Cloud provider shows partial fabric outage in us-west1-a/b. Control-plane reported flaps and backend health marked unhealthy.

sarah: Traffic-shift job kicked off to failover to us-east1 but the job shows many hosts still in draining state for >8m. connections not closing.

miguel: Logs from proxy: ``504 upstream read timeout, kv-cache flush stuck, waiting for chunks``. Looks like long-lived streams not terminating.

morgan: Customers on Dedicated capacity in us-west1 unaffected because they have pinned nodes. Hosted API is taking the hit. Estimated % of global requests failing ~18% from ingress metrics.

raj: DNS TTL is 30s, but some ISP caches are sticky. Also the global LB uses client affinity for some legacy routes which is preventing quick rehoming.

sarah: Trying graceful drain script on targets: ``/opt/redwood/bin/drain-host --timeout 60`` but script hangs on drain step for certain containers. Stack shows active KV sessions.

miguel: Can we force-terminate the connection pools on the proxy? There is a kill switch in proxy-config but it will drop in-flight requests. Need to weigh customer impact.

morgan: We should force-terminate for affected subnets (10.30.0.0/16) only. Can someone run the kill switch with a short notice?

raj: I can run it. Command: ``gcloud compute ssh proxy-agg-1 --zone=us-west1-b -- sudo /usr/local/bin/proxy-kill --target-subnet 10.30.0.0/16 --grace 5``. Running now.

deploy-bot: deploy started by raj at 2139998920: proxy-kill v1.3 -> affected nodes will drop connections.

sarah: Watching metrics... 1 minute... 2 minutes... 5xx rate dropping, p50 latency back to normal for shifted region. Still some request spikes into old region from certain CDNs.

miguel: We also need to update LB routing policy to prefer us-east1 for new connections. Changing weight from 50->90 for us-east1 in global-lb config.

morgan: Do it and share the command.

raj: ``gcloud compute forwarding-rules update global-api --region=us-east1 --set-traffic-weight=90`` executed at 2139999005.

sarah: DNS propagation still slow. Adding signed DNS override for critical endpoints in our edge-proxies so they resolve to us-east1 IPs immediately. Patch posted to edge-config and rolled to 3 nodes.

morgan: Heads-up: paging next 30m for oncall handoff. Oncall-ops are you taking the bridge in 15?

oncall-ops: taking handoff at 2140000100. I'll own until 2140003700. Confirmed.

miguel: Customer impact summary so far: Hosted API global request errors peaked at 28% for a 12m window, tail latency increased 4-5x for us-west origin clients. No data loss. Dedicated/reserved customers mostly unaffected.

morgan: Escalating to SRE leads for postmortem and potential routing policy changes (avoid client-affinity sticky routes). Tagging @product for customer comms.

raj: Postmortem checklist note: investigate draining blockers (kv-handle eviction), LB affinity config, and DNS fallback heuristics.

sarah: Will follow up with runbook edits: add explicit force-drain path and a low-risk proxy-kill SOP.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged. Bridge: https://zoom.redwood/incident-2139998888. Severity: SEV-2 -> owner: morgan, oncall: oncall-ops.

morgan: Temporary mitigation seems stable. Keeping this thread open for handoff notes and final impact numbers. I will update with timeline and next steps in 30m. :white_check_mark:
